root_cause.text: `skb_try_coalesce()` in `net/core/skbuff.c` failed to propagate `SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` when moving paged frags from one `sk_buff` to another, so an skb could retain shared/page-cache-backed frags without being marked as shared and later be modified in place unsafely.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `skb_try_coalesce()` “can attach paged frags from @from to @to” and that if `@from has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set`, “the shared-frag marker is currently lost,” which breaks `skb_has_shared_frag()` checks used by ESP before `skb_cow_data()`; the patch fixes this by adding `to_shinfo->flags |= from_shinfo->flags & SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG;` when `from_shinfo->nr_frags` is nonzero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve shared fragment flags when coalescing sk_buffs so fragment-sharing state remains correct.
intent_record.what: In skb_try_coalesce(), after adding from_shinfo->nr_frags to to_shinfo->nr_frags, the code now conditionally ORs to_shinfo->flags with from_shinfo->flags masked by SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when the source skb has any fragments.
intent_record.how: This preserves the shared-fragment flag during skb coalescing so the destination skb retains the correct fragment-sharing state after merging fragments from another skb.

grouping_result.intent: Preserve shared fragment flags when coalescing sk_buffs so fragment-sharing state remains correct.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes skb_try_coalesce() behavior by preserving SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when moving paged fragments, preventing shared frags from being left unmarked and later modified unsafely.

candidates.rationale: This coalescing step moves paged fragments from one skb to another, but in the vulnerable code it did not propagate the shared-fragment state along with the frags. As a result, the destination skb could contain shared/page-cache-backed frags without being marked accordingly.

This condition only handles clearing the source frag count when the source skb is not cloned; it does not address preserving SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG on the destination. The vulnerable logic allowed frag sharing state to be lost during coalescing.

After moving fragments, the source skb's frag count is cleared, but the corresponding shared-frag metadata was not propagated to the destination skb. This contributes to the inconsistent state that later permits unsafe in-place modification.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line moves paged fragments from the source skb into the destination skb, but in the vulnerable code it did so without propagating the shared-fragment state. That allowed the destination skb to retain shared/page-cache-backed frags without being marked with SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG, leading to unsafe in-place modification later.

This conditional only governs whether the source skb's fragment count is cleared. It does not preserve or transfer the shared-frag flag to the destination skb, which is the missing behavior at the root of the vulnerability.

This clears the source skb's fragment count after coalescing, but the vulnerable implementation failed to accompany that move with propagation of the shared-frag metadata to the destination skb. The resulting inconsistent state could leave shared frags unmarked and later modified unsafely.
